mbm-2151.clue: I lift beside the oldest mirror.
mbm-2151.quote: There's a chip in the glass exactly level with my collarbone. When I come up out of a squat I see that little star again. That's where I take my breath.

mbm-2152.clue: I paint a little weather on my hands.
mbm-2152.quote: My left thumb's the storm. On the right I put the cloud breaking up. Makes handing someone a cup of tea a much more interesting business.

mbm-2153.clue: My hook goes through the strawberry twice.
mbm-2153.quote: The fruit basket was supposed to be a year-end present. Then the kids got hold of my first red strawberry. Now I'm a full-time strawberry farmer with one hook.

mbm-2154.clue: I eat the peaches. My official counts the pits.
mbm-2154.quote: At the fair, we race to finish equal plates of peach halves. My official insists on counting the pits himself. Fair enough. He's six and it's his clipboard.

mbm-2155.clue: I brought the rain to our last screening.
mbm-2155.quote: Our club watched a silent anime short. I shook dry rice in a biscuit tin for the rain. Halfway through, real rain joined in on the roof. Perfect timing.

mbm-2156.clue: I wait for the train's shadow.
mbm-2156.quote: At noon the viaduct throws a neat ladder across the embankment. I lower my camera when the freight arrives. I want to see all those rungs fill up with wheels.

mbm-2157.clue: I save a square for emergencies.
mbm-2157.quote: The laundry line caught one corner of my quilt on a nail. I mended it with the lemon-yellow square I'd never found a place for. Best corner on the blanket now.

mbm-2158.clue: I play chess beside the sprinklers.
mbm-2158.quote: At five we both have to move, chessboard and all. My opponent remembers exactly where every piece stood. I remember which of us was losing when the water came on.

mbm-2159.clue: My favorite plates are the little ones.
mbm-2159.quote: I found a pair of tiny iron change plates in the gym's lost-and-found sale. They make the quietest possible clink. A small personal record deserves its own sound.

mbm-2160.clue: I waltz through a chalk puddle.
mbm-2160.quote: My partner draws something different on the studio floor every Monday. Last week it was an imaginary puddle. We glided right through it. I hated to mop it up.

mbm-2161.clue: I can throw through the moon.
mbm-2161.quote: We chalk a crescent on a big scrap of cardboard and cut it out. I get three tries to sail my disc through. The wind gets as many tries as it likes.

mbm-2162.clue: I bought our band's ugliest lamp.
mbm-2162.quote: The charity shop had a lamp shaped like a purple fish. We set it on my amp for our first gig. Now whenever we need to find the stage door we ask whoever's carrying the fish.

mbm-2163.quote: I rehearse the harmony in our stairwell. The woman above whistles the melody back through her door. We finally met on the landing and recognized each other halfway through hello.

mbm-2164.clue: I know which tent peg rang.
mbm-2164.quote: The ground at my favorite site is full of flat stones. Each peg makes its own sound going in. The high one by the spruce has been there for three summers.

mbm-2165.clue: I give the last life to my guest.
mbm-2165.quote: My old console still has the dent from the night we first beat the lighthouse level. Nobody remembers who dropped the controller. Everybody remembers the lighthouse.

mbm-2166.clue: I came for the wheels leaving the ground.
mbm-2166.quote: At the flying club I sit on the grass with a sketchbook. The instant daylight shows under both wheels I make one quick mark. My pages look like migrating birds.

mbm-2167.clue: I paddle with my lunch in a biscuit tin.
mbm-2167.quote: The tin makes a grand little table laid across the thwarts. At sunset I nose my canoe into the reeds and treat the dragonflies to a terrible view of my sandwich.

mbm-2168.clue: I lost the crown to a wooden sheep.
mbm-2168.quote: I hosted a game about running a tiny kingdom. The sheep was supposed to stand in for our missing king. By midnight we had voted to keep the sheep.

mbm-2169.clue: I take the early train for the benches.
mbm-2169.quote: The station cleaner paints one bench every spring. I ride the branch line out to see what color it is. This year it's the exact orange of my breakfast.

mbm-2170.clue: My first encore came out of a jam jar.
mbm-2170.quote: We put twenty song tokens in a jam jar and let the audience pick the encore. A little boy pulled out the one tune we'd only practiced backward as a joke. The crowd sang it forward for us.

mbm-2171.clue: I wanted my robot to kneel.
mbm-2171.quote: Every model on my shelf stood like it was waiting for a photograph. I spent a whole Sunday fitting one knee so my little machine could offer a child a flower.

mbm-2172.clue: I can change the moon in eight seconds.
mbm-2172.quote: Our theater has a different moon for every act. I swing the plywood crescent out and slide a fat yellow disk into its place. I swear the audience gasped for the moon once.

mbm-2173.clue: I leave room for the wrong ending.
mbm-2173.quote: I write the last page on a separate sheet and keep it in my sock drawer. By the time I get there my characters usually have a better idea. One even missed her own wedding.

mbm-2174.clue: I know a plane by the underside.
mbm-2174.quote: My spot by the end of the runway gives me about two seconds to sketch a passing belly. I shade the wings afterward from memory. The landing gear is always the giveaway.

mbm-2175.clue: I bring two folding stools to the park.
mbm-2175.quote: One is for me. The other is for the first stranger brave enough to sit down. My favorite opponent arrived with an ice cream and checkmated me before it dripped.
